answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation company blog post dated 2026-07-01 (publisher and speaker: NVIDIA; tier: party statement). It also quotes a Sharon AI CEO statement and Firmus executive statement, and reports Firmus Batam campus plans as stated by NVIDIA.
answer.note: NVIDIA's own statement, dated 2026-07-01, says it is introducing a business model in which AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers under a revenue-sharing and credit-support structure. As described, NVIDIA would earn standard product revenue plus a share of cloud revenue on supported capacity, which NVIDIA frames as a recurring, usage-linked earnings stream. This supports a conditional read that NVIDIA is extending its revenue model from hardware sales toward a share of downstream AI cloud revenue, with the structure aimed at helping AI clouds finance capital-intensive capacity. The source gives no revenue-share percentage, credit-support size, contract count, signing status or revenue timing, so it does not establish how material this model will be to NVIDIA's results. The Firmus Batam plan (expected to scale to 360 MW and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs) is a company-stated forward build-out by an AI cloud partner. It is a supply and demand lead for NVIDIA GPU capacity, not a disclosed NVIDIA order or purchase amount, and the GPU figure is an upper bound with no build timeline. The Sharon AI quote and the DSX AI factory references are qualitative partner and marketing statements that add no quantities.
limitations: The revenue-share percentage, credit-support amount and accounting treatment are not disclosed, so the size and timing of the economic effect on NVIDIA cannot be estimated from this source.

No signed agreements, named participating AI clouds beyond Sharon AI, Firmus and the referenced AI natives, or contract values are disclosed, so the status of the model's adoption is unknown rather than confirmed.
The Firmus campus figures (360 MW, up to 170,000 GPUs) are forward plans with no completion date, financing status or stated NVIDIA share of that capacity.

The source is NVIDIA's own promotional blog post and is not independently confirmed; the AI native customers named (Baseten, Fireworks AI, Together AI) are described as demand context, not as stated NVIDIA counterparties.
follow_up: Check NVIDIA's next 10-Q or 10-K and earnings commentary for any disclosure of the new model's revenue-share arrangements, credit guarantees, financing commitments or revenue recognition treatment.
Check Firmus Technologies and Sharon AI public filings or announcements for signed NVIDIA supply terms, financing close, GPU delivery schedules and Batam campus timing.
Check whether NVIDIA's filings disclose guarantees or credit-support obligations linked to AI cloud customers, since such obligations would bear on NVIDIA's contingent liabilities.
